The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Large irregular dark brown/black necrotic lesion at the top
- Marginal yellowing (chlorosis) along the edges
- A few smaller dark spots scattered on the leaf
- Overall green leaf with some discoloration

The large, irregular dark lesion with marginal yellowing is most suggestive of **Late Blight**. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Late Blight reference shows extensive dark brown/black necrotic areas spreading across the leaf — consistent with the pathogen *Phytophthora infestans*. The test image shows an earlier/more localized stage: a large irregular dark lesion at the leaf tip with marginal yellowing and a few scattered small spots — all consistent with Late Blight progression.

The test image pattern matches Late Blight well:
- Irregular dark necrotic lesion (not the concentric rings of Early Blight)
- Marginal chlorosis around affected areas
- Rapid-onset appearance without distinct target spots

This pattern is consistent with Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans): irregular water-soaked lesions turning dark without concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight), and without the white powdery coating (ruling out Powdery Mildew) or fine spots pattern (ruling out Septoria or Bacterial Speck). The reference Late Blight image confirms similar dark spreading necrosis."}
